The current directory doesn't contain the repo you're describing (glob turned up nothing), so I'll work from the description you gave and the folder-decision checklist, then flag what I need from you to finish the concrete file-by-file mapping.

## Diagnosis

Both folders fail the same check: **no single reason to change**. `misc` mixes five unrelated concerns (config, migrations, compliance archives, shared code, notes), and `utils` is a 30-file dumping ground with no organizing idea at all. Neither maps to one work-breakdown piece or one disposition rule, so nobody can predict where a new file belongs or what happens to an old one.

## Proposed structure

```
packages/shared/<domain>/     # kept — actively maintained shared code
scripts/migrations/           # archived — record of completed one-off runs
config/templates/             # kept — reusable, versioned templates
archive/compliance-reports/   # archived — read-only historical record
archive/meeting-notes/        # archived, likely deletable after a retention window
```

Mapping your description onto it:

| Content | Disposition | New home | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Config templates | kept | `config/templates/` | Reusable, versioned; changes with product config needs |
| One-off migration scripts | archived | `scripts/migrations/<iso-date>-<name>/` | Already run, kept for audit — not touched again |
| Archived compliance reports | archived | `archive/compliance-reports/` | Read-only history, own disposition rule |
| Shared helpers (2 services) | kept | `packages/shared/<domain>/`, split by what each helper does (e.g. `packages/shared/http-client/`, `packages/shared/date-formatting/`) — not one blob | Real shared code deserves ownership and cohesion, but "shared" isn't itself a domain |
| Old meeting notes | archived → likely delete | `archive/meeting-notes/<year>/`, or better, out of the code repo entirely (wiki/Drive) | Different reason to change than everything else in the repo — arguably shouldn't live in source control at all |

For `utils`, the fix is **dissolution, not a rename**: every file goes to one of two places, and `utils` disappears.

1. **Single-caller helpers** → move into the one service/module that uses them (colocate, least new structure).
2. **Genuinely cross-cutting helpers** → group by what they do under `packages/shared/<domain>/` (e.g. `strings/`, `dates/`, `http/`), each a cohesive folder with its own README. No bare `utils` anywhere going forward — that's an explicit red flag in this process.

Each non-trivial folder above (`packages/shared/*`, `scripts/migrations/`, `archive/*`) needs a short README stating purpose, what belongs, what doesn't, and disposition — otherwise this just becomes a slower-motion version of the same problem.

## Before I finalize this

Two things I need from you rather than guess:

1. **Does the repo already have a convention** for shared/internal code — `packages/`, `libs/`, `internal/`, something else? I don't want to invent a new root if one exists; I'd rather slot into it.
2. **The actual file lists** for `misc` and `utils` (or repo access). I can sort all 77 files into the categories above and produce the final outline-number → path map, but I can't do that accurately from category descriptions alone — some "shared helpers" may turn out to be single-caller, some "migration scripts" may still be live, etc.

Want to share the listing (or point me at the real repo path) so I can do the concrete sort?
